title: v1 param gateway + structured-response coercion for /v1/chat.completions
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: customers using OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions send a variety of historic parameters and role shapes. We need a thin, auditable gateway that: 1) normalizes legacy params (stop arrays, role aliases, max_tokens semantics) into Redwood runtime config, 2) coerces and annotates the structured response envelope for function/tool calling so downstream consumers see consistent fields, and 3) preserves/logs logprobs and stop signals during streaming without degrading latency. This PR implements a v1 param gateway and a response coercion layer.

What this changes (high level): normalizer: new component that validates and rewrites incoming /v1 payloads into internal canonical proto; stop-array handling: converts openai style stop arrays into our stop-priority list and attaches deterministic tie-break hints; role aliasing: maps common aliases (assistant/bot/system/helper) into canonical roles while keeping original_role metadata for observability; logprobs & streaming: ensure per-token logprob buckets are propagated in the framed streaming envelope and add fallback behavior to synthesize token-level logprobs when upstream model doesn't supply them (configurable); structured output: add optional response_coercion hint that converts free-form function call output into our framed JSON tool-output object with provenance fields.

Checklist:
- [x] v1 param gateway implementation (validation + rewrite)
- [x] Structured-response coercion with provenance annotations
- [x] Preserve role metadata in logs and telemetry
- [x] Streaming envelope compatibility tests for logprobs and stop events
- [x] Unit tests for param permutations and backcompat
- [x] Integration tests against openai-compat harness
- [x] Docs snippet for /v1/chat.completions differences and migration notes

Backward compatibility: This is designed to be additive and opt-in for existing v1 clients. The gateway runs before routing and can be disabled via feature flag if a downstream customer needs raw passthrough. No breaking change to existing internal runtime API contracts is intended (see release_notes).

release_notes: Add a v1 parameter gateway that normalizes OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parameters into Redwood runtime config, introduces structured-response coercion to standardize function/tool outputs, and preserves logprob/stop information in streaming envelopes. Opt-in via feature flag; see docs/openai_v1_migration.md for migration steps and caveats.
